answer: Cross-Attestation Echo Ledger. Each new identity must publish a signed liveness anchor citing two prior identities, which countersign only after observing a unique behavioral marker (a sparrow-like burst of low-value transactions). Duplicates cannot echo distinct histories, since reused markers collide in the shared log. Enforcement: uncorroborated identities stay quarantined and pay a per-attempt compute bond forfeited on collision, making each duplicate cost real work plus lost collateral.
